name: FR. POLYNESIA
lead: French Polynesia has 121 islands in the South Pacific. Volcanic peaks tower over clear lagoons, and atolls (rings of coral) sit barely above the sea. The word tattoo was born here, and black pearls grow here too.
geo: The 121 islands spread over an ocean zone bigger than Europe. The tallest peak, Orohena on Tahiti, soars to 2,241 m. The Marquesas islands have steep sea cliffs.
The Tuamotu islands form the largest chain of coral atolls on Earth. Bora Bora's emerald volcano rises from a turquoise lagoon.
animals: Humpback whales give birth here from July to November. Reef manta rays glide like underwater kites at Bora Bora, where small fish clean them, nearly all year.
The Tahiti monarch is a tiny black bird found nowhere else on Earth, and it is critically endangered. Bright blue lorikeet parrots flit through coconut palms on remote atolls.
culture: The word tattoo comes from Polynesian tatu. Inked patterns tell family histories. Every July, dancers fill the month-long Heiva i Tahiti festival.
Farmers grow black pearls in black-lip oysters in the Tuamotu lagoons. Pearls are the islands' biggest export. Islanders live by aita pea pea, meaning 'no worries'.
history: Polynesian voyagers settled the islands around the year 300, steering by the stars. British captain Samuel Wallis reached Tahiti in 1767, and the French explorer Bougainville followed a year later.
France took over the islands in 1880. From 1966 to 1996, it set off 193 nuclear weapons in the Tuamotu atolls. Today the islands govern themselves within France.
wows: The 121 islands are as spread out as London to Moscow.
Captain Cook's sailors brought tatu home in 1769, and it became tattoo.
A Tahitian black pearl takes up to two years to grow.
Bora Bora's lagoon is so vivid that WWII soldiers thought it was unreal.
France set off 193 nuclear weapons here, 46 of them above ground.
The islands' ocean zone covers 5 million km², huge for so little land.
Near Moorea island, you can snorkel beside a humpback mother and calf.

myths.myth: Coral reefs are made of rock and plants
myths.fact: Coral is made of tiny animals called polyps. They build their stony homes over thousands of years.
Storms can hit from November to April. Big swells can flood low atolls.
